stem: For `Statevector.from_label('10')` on a two-qubit system, which computational-basis amplitude is 1?

options.text: Index 2 — labels read |q1 q0⟩, so qubit 1 is the one that is set
Index 1 — reading left to right, '10' sets qubit 0 = 1 and qubit 1 = 0
It raises an error — `from_label` may only be given a single character

explanation.correct: `from_label` reads the string left-to-right as |q_{n-1} … q_0⟩. So '10' means qubit 1 = 1, qubit 0 = 0, which is the basis state with integer index 2 (binary 10). The amplitude at index 2 is 1.

distractors.D: This reverses the label order. The leftmost character is the highest-index qubit, so '10' has qubit 1 = 1 (index 2), not qubit 0 = 1 (index 1).
distractors.A: |11⟩ (index 3) would come from label '11'. '10' has a 0 on qubit 0.
distractors.E: Single-qubit-label misconception: `Statevector.from_label` accepts multi-character labels (and '+', '-', 'r', 'l' too), building one qubit per character.

provenance.notes: length tell cleared (correct trimmed, distractor D spells out the reversed reading) | pool wave: +E single-character-label misconception for from_label
